content:
- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is bullish (high sentiment scores) — adjust downward by 1–2% for the first 5–7 days.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is bearish (low sentiment scores) — add 1–2% to forecast for the first 5–7 days.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in sentiment — cap forecast at +3% above peak for 3–5 days.
- Lagged price movements (e.g., 10–15 day delays) are consistently overpredicted — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for each lagged period.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — if price moves >5% above 30-day average, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from bullish to bearish) triggers underprediction — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for 2–4 days after sentiment drop.
- Forecast horizon >14 days shows persistent bias — apply 1–2% downward correction for long-term forecasts when sentiment is neutral or declining.
